question: How should I deal with guilt and waswasa that I'm not reciting the Qur'an properly?
asked: A sister is getting waswasa or doubts when she's reading the Qur'an: she feels that she's not good enough, that she's not doing a good enough job, that she's not reciting it properly, and sometimes that she's not giving the Qur'an its haqq and not making tadabbur.
answer:
And the response: to a certain level, these feelings are very positive. If these feelings impede your act of worship, they become negative, okay? So to feel guilty at not perfecting the recitation of the Qur'an, to feel guilty that you're not doing a good enough job, that's actually very good. We should all feel an element of guilt. Our salahs... I mean, we should all feel guilty that our khushu' is not the way it should be, that our punctuality is not the way that it should be, that other things are not the way... Excellent. To feel that guilt is a sign of iman. The moment we don't feel guilty, the moment that we feel, "Oh, I am doing this perfectly," that is in fact an element of arrogance, and that is dangerous, and we do not want that. **So to feel guilty at a certain level is positive.**

If that guilt increases to the point that she cannot even do her action of worship, to the point that she's not even wanting to do her action of worship, to the point that she decides, "I'd rather not do the Qur'an than feel this amount of guilt," then realize that this feeling of healthy guilt has been corrupted by Shaytan, and it has become what we call a waswasa. And a waswasa is a whispering of Shaytan that is meant to invalidate the action of worship. And when this feeling of waswasa gets to the level of impeding an action of worship, that is when we need to cut it short and realize this is a tactic of Shaytan. This is a tactic of Shaytan that he used for our father Adam:

> فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا الشَّيْطَانُ

So to continually doubt. And that's why we seek refuge in Allah, that we seek refuge from the waswas of the one who steals and throws thoughts into us. He is the one who ruins our actions of worship because of the waswas. That's what this khannas does. And that is why we have to be careful.

What you asked me, in and of itself, it seems as if she is in category one. She is saying, "I'm feeling guilty, I'm not concentrating enough." As for feeling guilty that you're not concentrating enough, that is good. But don't let it stop you from attempting to concentrate, right? Don't let it stop you from trying to do better.

As for the feeling of guilt at not reciting the Qur'an properly with tajweed, let me give you good news. Our Prophet ﷺ said, "The one who recites the Qur'an fluently is in the company of the noble angels. And the one who recites the Qur'an," the one who stumbles, the one who's making differences in the harakat, and it's difficult for him, the Prophet ﷺ said, "for that one, he shall get the double reward." He shall get the double reward because he is not fluent, yet he's struggling and trying. He's struggling, making a mistake, going back, reading it again. So he's still attempting. For that attempt, he shall get a double reward. So do not feel guilty that your tajweed is not on par. Alhamdulillah, you get a double reward.

But then try your best to learn tajweed. Try your best to attend classes. This is the ideal time; alhamdulillah, you have some extra time now with this lockdown. Find some teachers online. There are Qur'an halaqas that we do at EPIC as well. I know the sisters have a Qur'an halaqa as well. So sign up, see what you can do. Improve your tajweed. And you know, tajweed is a very, very, very simple science. It is the easiest science of Islam. Wallahi, it is the easiest science of Islam. Simple rules: see what is the letter, see what is before, see what is after. And then you will find yourself improving within 10, 20 minutes of learning a rule. You're going to implement it, and then another rule, and then another rule, and then you keep on practicing. And you will find that, insha'Allah ta'ala, you will improve your tajweed very, very easily. So try your best to learn the rules of tajweed, and find a teacher. And we have at EPIC as well a sisters' halaqa of Qur'an. So do what you can to do that. May Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala bless you in that regard.
